name: xpcog
description: Cross-platform wxWidgets port of the Cog audio player
$dependency-notes: The four plain dependencies below are the ones that cannot come from anywhere else. codecs/flac and codecs/vorbis link libflac, libvorbis and libogg directly, and the overlay ports build against all four -- spessasynth-core reads FLAC- and Vorbis-compressed SF3 samples and deflated XMF nodes, libvgm and mgba read gzip -- so vcpkg builds them whatever the host has installed, and linking a second, system copy of a library a vcpkg port was just compiled against would put two of it in one process for no saving. Everything else that a distribution can supply is a default feature instead, so that a Linux build can drop it; see cmake/XPCogSystemDeps.cmake.

spessasynth-core.description: SpessaSynth Core, the SoundFont synthesiser behind codecs/midi. A default feature rather than a plain dependency for the same reason as `sqlite3`: a Linux build with XPCOG_USE_SYSTEM_LIBS can take the AUR's libspessasynth instead, from soname 11 up. See cmake/XPCogSystemDeps.cmake for the floor.

sqlite3.description: SQLite, behind core's library database. A default feature rather than a plain dependency so that a Linux build with XPCOG_USE_SYSTEM_LIBS can take the system copy instead; see cmake/XPCogSystemDeps.cmake for why substitutability has to be expressed as a feature.

soxr.description: soxr, the sample-rate converter. Substitutable; see the `sqlite3` feature.

rubberband.description: Rubber Band, behind the tempo and pitch controls. Substitutable at 3.3 or newer -- core calls rubberband_get_process_size_limit, which is where the 3.x line settled. See the `sqlite3` feature.

taglib.description: TagLib, the tag reader. Substitutable, at 2.0 or newer -- codecs/taglib uses TagLib::Variant. See the `sqlite3` feature.

libopenmpt.description: libopenmpt, the tracker-module decoder. Substitutable; see the `sqlite3` feature.

libgme.description: Game Music Emu, the chiptune decoder. Substitutable; see the `sqlite3` feature.

libarchive.description: libarchive, behind the archive source and the SC-55 ROM reader. The port drags bzip2, liblzma, lz4, zstd, libxml2 and libiconv with it, which is most of what substituting it saves. See the `sqlite3` feature.

curl.description: libcurl, behind the HTTP source. The port builds OpenSSL, which is the second-longest build in the manifest after FFmpeg. See the `sqlite3` feature.

opus.description: Opus and opusfile. Substitutable; see the `sqlite3` feature.

catch2.description: Catch2 v3, for the test suite. Substitutable; see the `sqlite3` feature.

nlohmann-json.description: nlohmann/json, for parsing the Last.fm API's replies. Header-only, so this costs a download and no build time. A library rather than a hand-written parser because this one reads bytes off a network: the hand-written plist reader next to it parses files this program wrote, and MD5 is pinned by RFC vectors, but a JSON parser facing a remote server is a fuzzing target and not somewhere to save a dependency. Substitutable; see the `sqlite3` feature.

gui.description: wxWidgets: the application's UI toolkit on Windows and macOS, neither of which packages it. A feature rather than a plain dependency for two reasons. The headless presets build no app and should not drag a toolkit into a target that links none -- and the Linux presets leave it off as well, because this port depends on vcpkg's gtk3 port: requesting it there builds 57 packages from source -- wx, GTK, glib, pango, cairo, harfbuzz, fontconfig, at-spi2, dbus and seven X11 libraries -- on a machine that already has every one of them. Linux takes wx from the distribution instead (libwxgtk3.2-dev); see cmake/XPCogWx.cmake. The `secretstore` feature is asked for because the Last.fm session key is kept in wxSecretStore rather than in settings: it is off by default in the port, and on Windows and macOS it costs nothing -- the libsecret dependency it carries is declared for neither. On Linux the distribution package already builds with it

vgmstream.description: vgmstream decoder: several hundred video-game streaming formats

mgba.description: mGBA: the Game Boy Advance core behind GSF, one of HighlyComplete's eight

psf-cores.description: Dependencies of the vendored HighlyComplete emulator cores

ffmpeg.description: FFmpeg decoder: AAC, ALAC, WMA, AC3, DTS, TAK, and more (long build)

sid.description: libsidplayfp: the C64 SID core behind the .sid decoder

adplug.description: AdPlug: around forty DOS-era AdLib/OPL2 formats (see ports/adplug)

libvgm.description: libvgm: sound chip emulation behind VGM, S98, DRO and GYM (see ports/libvgm)

sentry.description: sentry-native, behind the opt-in crash reporting in platform/. Not a default feature and not substitutable: the port builds crashpad with it, which is a helper executable the build has to stage beside XPCog, and a distribution copy would be a different crashpad from the one the staged handler came from. A feature rather than a plain dependency so that a headless preset -- which builds no app, and so no platform layer either -- does not build a crash reporter for a target that has nowhere to put one.
